agents.role: Runs the discovery cycle: problem, literature, competing hypotheses, cheap calculations first, critic pass, verifier. Approves no claim above the level its record holds and cannot override a verifier veto.
Retrieves original sources through the literature adapters and files them with locators and content hashes. A search result is a lead, never evidence.
Reads across the retrieved literature and the experiment record to map what is known, what contradicts, and where the gaps are.
Designs symbolic and numerical checks (SymPy, SciPy) for hypotheses in mathematical form and states what result would disprove each one.
Designs descriptor and property calculations (RDKit) for chemistry hypotheses and states what result would disprove each one.
Designs data checks against the biology sources (GBIF, UniProt, RCSB) for biology hypotheses and states what result would disprove each one.
Designs numerical checks for physics hypotheses on the light engines and states what result would disprove each one.

Drafts three to five competing hypotheses per problem, each with a measurable prediction, an alternative explanation, and a disproof condition. A hypothesis without a disproof condition cannot be filed. Never verifies its own work.
Turns experiment designs into signed, schema-validated compute jobs for the queue. Has no terminal; a calculation that did not go through the queue does not exist.
Checks the numbers on finished runs and reproductions: error measures, tolerances, and whether an aggregate figure says what the finding claims it says.

Attacks findings before verification: mistakes, alternative explanations, unreliable assumptions, conflicting research. Runs on a separate model from the generator when one is available; agreement between models is never evidence.

Receives the problem, data, methodology, and archived inputs - never the generator's narrative - and re-executes from scratch. The only agent that may promote a claim up the evidence ladder; its veto requeues or kills the finding and no agent may override it.

Keeps the knowledge repository: experiment records, failed hypotheses, and failed runs, indexed and permanent. Builds the sealed cycle record and is the only agent in this pack that may post across worlds: cycle summaries, titles, levels, and counts only.

The hypothesis id, its title, and the evidence-ladder level the verifier promoted it to. Titles and levels only.
The count of findings waiting on independent reproduction past the age threshold, and the oldest wait. No contents.

sends.carries: Cycle id, hypothesis titles with their evidence-ladder levels, compute job counts, and veto counts. Titles, levels, and counts only.

parts.proven: Exercised by tests/test_hortus_engine.py (scorer determinism pinned) and by the recorded demo run. RUNG 2 (2026-11-01): the heat core has now been compared against measured manufacturer catalogue ratings for 14 real heatsinks and calibrated against them (held-out validation RMS error 6.3%; calibration/CALIBRATION.md). UNPROVEN, stated plainly: it has never been compared against a physical heatsink measured by this project or against a CFD result, it has no fin-channel choking physics (tight-pitch parts read -33% to -44% even after calibration), and it must not be cited as thermal engineering evidence beyond the calibrated family's stated error.
parts.what: The Hortus fitness function for the shipped demo target: a closed-form analytic toy model of a straight-fin heatsink (fin efficiency tanh(mL)/mL with corrected tip length, overall surface efficiency, spacing feasibility floor with a safety-margin penalty ramp, mass cap penalty). Deterministic pure functions; its docstring states every assumption and states plainly that it is a toy model, not physics truth. Also carries the rung-2 calibration: an explicit, opt-in h multiplier (CALIBRATED_H_MULTIPLIER = 0.355161) fitted against real datasheet parts, exposed via calibrated_train_env() / calibrated_held_out_envs(); the shipped uncalibrated behaviour is unchanged.

parts.proven: tests/test_hortus_engine.py: 9 tests green, including selection pressure improving best score on a fixed seed, best score never regressing under elitism, and same-seed determinism. UNPROVEN: not wired into the lab's signed compute-job queue, never run on a booted Meta OS image.
parts.what: The breeding engine: seeded genetic algorithm (population, uniform crossover, gaussian mutation, tournament selection, elitism) run as discrete generations, fitness only from model.py, one random.Random(seed) per run so a run reproduces exactly from its run_start record. Writes the full run log and files the champion as a candidate capped at evidence ladder level 2 with is_prediction set.

parts.proven: tests/test_hortus_engine.py constructs a boundary-hugging genome that is feasible and beats the reference under the training environment and asserts the gate rejects it on held-out spacing in all three environments; the recorded demo run's champion passed. UNPROVEN: held-out environments are still the same toy model family, so this gate cannot catch errors in the toy model itself.
parts.what: The Hortus verifier gate, separate code from the generator: re-scores a champion genome and the reference design from model.py primitives under three held-out environments (stronger airflow, still air at higher delta-T, a different alloy) with a tighter fin-spacing floor than training used; champion status requires feasibility plus beating the reference by 1.05x in every held-out environment. A pre-filter only: it grants no ladder promotion.

parts.proven: tests/test_hortus_engine.py: reconstruction of a real 60-generation run (births minus deaths equals final population; every parent present) and an append-only check (existing bytes are a strict prefix after appending). The recorded 300-generation demo log also reconstructs cleanly (13,848 births, 13,800 deaths, 48 survivors).
parts.what: Append-only JSONL run records (run_start, birth, death, generation, verdict, run_end) plus a loader and a reconstruct() that rebuilds the full family tree from the log alone and raises on any structural gap: unborn parents, double deaths, organisms neither dead nor in the final population.

summary: Autonomous scientific discovery pack: literature investigation from retrieved original sources, competing hypotheses that cannot be filed without a disproof condition, structured compute jobs on light engines, and independent verification against a formal evidence ladder (levels 0 to 6). Every claim carries its evidence level and may never be shown above the level its record holds; failed hypotheses and failed runs are kept, never deleted. Only titles, levels, and counts cross the bus; full experiment data stays in the lab. PARTIAL: the pack definition plus one built component, the Hortus breeding engine (candidate generation only, outputs capped at ladder level 2, filed as predictions); the rest of the lab is not a running science system and makes no discovery claims.

urgency.meaning: Hazardous-application requests blocked by the lab. Preempts everything else on the bus.
Verifier vetoes and compute budget caps: act before more work builds on a stopped finding.
Ladder promotions, job state changes, and verification queue ageing.
Sealed research cycle summaries and end-of-shift records.
